evidence.description: DateFormatter is instantiated inside the computed property 'localizedMonthAndYear', which can lead to performance overhead if accessed frequently.
DateFormatter is instantiated inside the 'fetchAndUpdate' method, which is executed every time the data is fetched.

candidates.explanation: DateFormatter is an expensive object to create. Instantiating it inside a computed property or a frequently called method is a common performance anti-pattern in Swift.
candidates.title: Inefficient DateFormatter instantiation

evidence.description: The timeZone is set using the abbreviation 'GMT'.
The timeZone is set using the abbreviation 'UTC'.

candidates.explanation: Using abbreviations like 'GMT' or 'UTC' to initialize a TimeZone can be unreliable as abbreviations can be ambiguous or vary by region. It is generally safer to use identifier strings like 'GMT' or 'UTC' or specific TimeZone objects.
candidates.title: Hardcoded TimeZone abbreviation

evidence.description: The data is first converted to a dictionary using JSONSerialization.
The dictionary is then converted back to Data using JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject:) to be decoded by JSONDecoder.

candidates.explanation: The code converts JSON data into a dictionary and then back into Data just to use JSONDecoder. This is inefficient and can be avoided by decoding the structure directly from the initial data.
